skill.name: pdf-processing-pro
skill.description: Production-ready PDF processing guidance for forms, tables, OCR, validation, and batch workflows. It includes usage examples and one form analysis script for extracting PDF field metadata.
skill.summary: Process PDF forms, tables, OCR text, and batch document workflows with practical Python examples.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown fences, example PDF output writes, ordinary glob usage, and safe subprocess examples. Two OCR installation examples are confirmed because they instruct users to run sudo apt-get install, which requires elevated privileges and should require explicit user approval.

remediation.issue: OCR setup examples use sudo apt-get install commands.
remediation.suggestion: Mark system package installation as a manual prerequisite and instruct agents to ask for confirmation before running privileged commands.

remediation.issue: Documentation references helper scripts that are not present in the scanned file tree.
remediation.suggestion: Either include the referenced scripts or clarify which examples are templates that users must implement themselves.

remediation.issue: Example output paths may overwrite existing local files if reused without checking.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend writing to a dedicated output directory and checking for existing files before batch processing.

content.value_statement: Complex PDF work often requires separate tools for forms, OCR, tables, and validation. This skill gives Claude Code, Claude, and Codex practical workflows for production PDF processing.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to analyze PDF form fields and export field metadata.
Shows workflows for filling, validating, flattening, and batching PDF forms.
Guides table extraction from PDFs with CSV, Excel, and JSON export patterns.
Provides OCR setup and preprocessing examples for scanned PDF text extraction.
Includes one runnable analyze_form.py script for PDF form metadata extraction.
Documents error handling, exit codes, logging, and batch processing practices.
limitations: Only analyze_form.py is included in the scanned files; other scripts are documented examples.
OCR workflows require separate Tesseract and Python package installation.
Scanned, encrypted, malformed, or XFA-based PDFs may need additional tooling.
Examples require user-provided PDFs and local filesystem output paths.

use_cases.title: Automate application form processing
use_cases.description: Analyze a PDF form, validate submission data, fill fields, and create completed documents.

use_cases.title: Extract report tables for analysis
use_cases.description: Pull tabular data from financial, operational, or research reports into structured files.

use_cases.title: Convert scanned documents to searchable text
use_cases.description: Use OCR preprocessing and language settings to extract text from image-based PDFs.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a PDF form
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the PDF Processing Pro skill to inspect my PDF form and explain the fields, required values, and recommended output structure.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a table extraction workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a workflow for extracting tables from a monthly report PDF into CSV files with validation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Improve OCR accuracy
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the OCR guidance in this skill to propose preprocessing steps for a scanned PDF with low contrast and mixed English and Spanish text.

prompt_templates.title: Build a batch PDF pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Use PDF Processing Pro to outline a safe batch pipeline for hundreds of PDFs, including validation, logging, output directories, and failure handling.

output_examples.input: Analyze this application form PDF and tell me what data I need to fill it.
output: A list of detected fields grouped by type.
Recommended validation rules before filling the form.

output_examples.input: Extract tables from this report and prepare them for spreadsheet review.
output: Suggested extraction settings for the PDF layout.
A CSV or Excel export plan.
Post-processing checks for headers, empty cells, and numeric values.

output_examples.input: Create an OCR plan for scanned invoices.
output: Quality checks for confidence, missing text, and page-level errors.

best_practices: Validate PDF paths, output directories, and expected fields before processing documents.
Test workflows on a small sample before running large batch jobs.
Keep original PDFs unchanged and write results to a separate output directory.
anti_patterns: Do not run privileged package installation commands without explicit user approval.
Do not assume all PDFs support editable AcroForm fields or reliable table extraction.
Do not overwrite generated PDFs or extracted data without checking existing files first.

faq.question: Does this skill include runnable scripts?
faq.answer: The scanned package includes analyze_form.py. Other script names are documented workflow examples and may need implementation.

faq.question: Can it process scanned PDFs?
faq.answer: Yes, the OCR guide explains Tesseract-based extraction and image preprocessing for scanned documents.

faq.question: Can it fill PDF forms?
faq.answer: The documentation shows form filling patterns with pypdf, validation, and flattening. A complete fill script was not present in the scanned files.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. Claude Code can use the guidance and the included form analysis script in local PDF workflows.

faq.question: What permissions should I expect?
faq.answer: Normal workflows read PDFs and write output files. OCR setup may require manual system package installation.

faq.question: What PDF types are difficult?
faq.answer: Encrypted PDFs, damaged files, scanned images with poor quality, and XFA forms may require extra tools or manual review.
